147: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-tactics-doombringer",
148: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok",
149: 	name = _t"orbital base: battle plan (doombringer)",
150: 	template = true,
151: 	lore = _t[=[Engagement Briefing on <?=player.name?>:
152: 
153: This slippery little <?=_t(player.descriptor.subrace, "birth descriptor name")?> has proven to be a thorn in our side so far.  We've reinforced our wards to better protect against the sort of fluke meteor impact that enabled <?=player:his_her()?> escape, but the crystal <?=player:he_she()?> smashed on <?=player:his_her()?> way out prevented us from keeping track of <?=player:his_her()?> location directly.  No matter - the brands and marks we've imbued <?=player:him_her()?> with have nonetheless allowed us to monitor magical energy signals affecting <?=player:him_her()?>, and our scryers have noted that there appears to be a particular pattern that teleports <?=player:him_her()?>, possibly of Sher'Tul origin.  We've sent out a signal of our own to intercept this, and redirect it to our platform, where <?=player:he_she()?> will be safely secured, punished for <?=player:his_her()?> disobedience, then once again exposed to a Tablet of Enlightenment to regain <?=player:his_her()?> servitude.
154: 
155: That said, given that <?=player:he_she()?> has increased dramatically in power since <?=player:his_her()?> escape, it is crucial that we keep proper tactics in mind.  Having been exposed to our alteration magic, <?=player:he_she()?> is very formidable in direct melee combat, and in the event that we cannot procure proper warding against this magic before <?=player:his_her()?> arrival, <?=player:he_she()?> can cause significant damage if not properly handled.  Under no circumstances should we let <?=player:him_her()?> run rampant in our back line; furthermore, if we simply try to lure <?=player:him_her()?> into a narrow corridor, we will not be able to bring enough firepower to bear before <?=player:he_she()?> can break through our obstructions.  Instead, use a small flanking squad backed up by a maulotaur (or whatever high-power direct combatant we can get authorization to deploy) to force <?=player:him_her()?> into an open area, where we'll have caster artillery, protected by a front-line of wretchlings backed by quasits.  We may lose these front-line soldiers, but in the time it takes <?=player:him_her()?> to slash <?=player:his_her()?> way through them, our spells should be able to reduce <?=player:him_her()?> to a flayed, quivering wreck.
156: 
157: Above all else, remember: despite <?=player:his_her()?> brute strength, this is a pitiful, inferior Eyalite who lucked <?=player:his_her()?> way into obtaining some of our superior power.  <?=player:he_she():capitalize()?> does not know how to use it properly, and does not have the countless years of experience with it that we do.  We have numbers, familiarity, tactics, and the blessing of Urh'Rok himself.  Treat this like a drill; if we stay calm and focused, it is unlikely we will see any casualties.
158: ]=]

295: 	lore = _t[=[Behold, the humble wretchling, a testament to our devotion to our Father!  These children of emerald were among the first to alter themselves for our quest for vengeance, and managed an astounding degree of success.  With their bursts of blinding speed, overwhelming numbers, and skin that can release prodigious amounts of corrosive fluid, wretchlings can storm onto the battlefield and pounce on our foes one-by-one, dissolving the ground they walk on while leaving them helpless against our onslaught.  Wretchlings will readily give their lives in combat, serving as obstructions and shields while their acid and our casters do their work, and still remain the most populous of our species thanks to their incredible birth rates.  It is rare to see a wretchling survive to maturity, but make no mistake - every wretchling that fights does an incredible service to our cause.]=]

301: 	name = _t"demon statue: fire imp",
302: 	lore = _t[=[If the Wretchling speaks to our worship, the Fire Imp speaks to our commitment and loyalty.  When a child of ruby goes out onto the battlefield, she fuses some of the Eyal-scarred earth from our planet to her hands, having perfected a type of magic that uses the raging magic contained within to blast our foes with the fires they've caused.  Aside from this means of appropriate justice being pleasing to Urh'Rok (as he showed when dealing with the dust-mages), it shows how dedicated we are to our cause: without hands, there's very little a Fire Imp would be able to do if she deserted or became demoralized.  Fighting and destroying is what we live for, and what better way to show it than making oneself unable to do anything but fight and destroy?  Although the bulk of the ruby species do not pursue this path, instead focusing on magical research and furthering our alteration projects, the example that the Fire Imp sets is a shining standard of commitment for all of Urh'Rok's children.]=]

135: "It's your lucky day, <?=player.name?>," your handler says as he leads you to a large, glowing crystal.  "You're too cooperative to stay in testing any longer.  Today, you're getting promoted to research assistant!"  You're nearly beside yourself with joy!  "Now, we'll need to do a short little process first.  Fireproofing wards here, loyalty reinforcement there, standard-issue alteration, but mostly just linking your consciousness to this," he says, pointing to the crystal.  "With this thing, everything you see, hear, smell, taste, or feel gets fed directly into this little ol' beauty.  Not just that, either - whereever you go, and whatever you think, we'll have it saved for future reference."  You're going to help them learn so much!  "Just step on the plate here, and hold your arms like this so I can get the bindings in place..."
136: 
137: That crystal.  That crystal is how they're keeping track of you, and it has most of what you helped them discover trapped within it.  If you break it, you'll be able to escape their notice for the first time since you arrived here, allowing you to get away without them finding you again, and as an added bonus you'll undo most of what you helped them accomplish.  You need to destroy it, then flee for your life!]=]

147: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-tactics-doombringer",
148: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok",
149: 	name = _t"orbital base: battle plan (doombringer)",
150: 	template = true,
151: 	lore = _t[=[Engagement Briefing on <?=player.name?>:
152: 
153: This slippery little <?=_t(player.descriptor.subrace, "birth descriptor name")?> has proven to be a thorn in our side so far.  We've reinforced our wards to better protect against the sort of fluke meteor impact that enabled <?=player:his_her()?> escape, but the crystal <?=player:he_she()?> smashed on <?=player:his_her()?> way out prevented us from keeping track of <?=player:his_her()?> location directly.  No matter - the brands and marks we've imbued <?=player:him_her()?> with have nonetheless allowed us to monitor magical energy signals affecting <?=player:him_her()?>, and our scryers have noted that there appears to be a particular pattern that teleports <?=player:him_her()?>, possibly of Sher'Tul origin.  We've sent out a signal of our own to intercept this, and redirect it to our platform, where <?=player:he_she()?> will be safely secured, punished for <?=player:his_her()?> disobedience, then once again exposed to a Tablet of Enlightenment to regain <?=player:his_her()?> servitude.
154: 
155: That said, given that <?=player:he_she()?> has increased dramatically in power since <?=player:his_her()?> escape, it is crucial that we keep proper tactics in mind.  Having been exposed to our alteration magic, <?=player:he_she()?> is very formidable in direct melee combat, and in the event that we cannot procure proper warding against this magic before <?=player:his_her()?> arrival, <?=player:he_she()?> can cause significant damage if not properly handled.  Under no circumstances should we let <?=player:him_her()?> run rampant in our back line; furthermore, if we simply try to lure <?=player:him_her()?> into a narrow corridor, we will not be able to bring enough firepower to bear before <?=player:he_she()?> can break through our obstructions.  Instead, use a small flanking squad backed up by a maulotaur (or whatever high-power direct combatant we can get authorization to deploy) to force <?=player:him_her()?> into an open area, where we'll have caster artillery, protected by a front-line of wretchlings backed by quasits.  We may lose these front-line soldiers, but in the time it takes <?=player:him_her()?> to slash <?=player:his_her()?> way through them, our spells should be able to reduce <?=player:him_her()?> to a flayed, quivering wreck.
156: 
157: Above all else, remember: despite <?=player:his_her()?> brute strength, this is a pitiful, inferior Eyalite who lucked <?=player:his_her()?> way into obtaining some of our superior power.  <?=player:he_she():capitalize()?> does not know how to use it properly, and does not have the countless years of experience with it that we do.  We have numbers, familiarity, tactics, and the blessing of Urh'Rok himself.  Treat this like a drill; if we stay calm and focused, it is unlikely we will see any casualties.
158: ]=]
159: }

191: That said, given that <?=player:he_she()?> has increased dramatically in power since <?=player:his_her()?> escape, it is crucial that we keep proper tactics in mind.  Our standard alterations have synergized with this Shalore's natural reactive magic, giving <?=player:him_her()?> short-range teleportation to rival Draebor and creating a frustratingly evasive target to hit. 468: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-demon-statue-general_of_urh_rok",
469: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
470: 	name = _t"demon statue: Khulmanar, General of Urh'Rok",
471: 	lore = _t[=[Our tournaments, run ever since our salvation from the dust mages under the command and inspiration of Urh'Rok, are not simply tests of direct combat, as many may think.  We have those, yes, but we also have competitions for scholarly work, attentiveness, physical endurance, philosophy, and countless other fields.  Perhaps the most prestigious of these, though, is the Divine Tournament of Tactics, by which our military leaders are selected.  Through a series of trials, we are compared in our abilities to assess a combat scenario and swiftly handle it, rated on speed, casualties, deployment efficiency, and a variety of other factors.  Khulmanar, a child of onyx, is the reigning champion of these, and has been for most of the time that we've spent waiting for our continent to reach Eyal.  Chosen by our process as the wisest tactical mind among our people, he was selected to meet with Urh'Rok himself to gain his approval to lead our forces in the invasion.  Urh'Rok was so impressed by Khulmanar that he used a significant portion of the little energy he's not using to hold our world together to build Khulmanar a new body, one strong enough to let him direct battles from the front-line without fear.  With a form and weapons granted by our Father, and a mind given his direct, enthusiastic approval, Khulmanar is considered to be the avatar of Urh'Rok, and his commands in battle are to be treated with the same reverence we would give to the words of Father himself.]=]
472: }

475: 	id = "ashes-urhrok-demon-statue-lithfengel",
476: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
477: 	name = _t"demon statue: Lithfengel",
478: 	lore = _t[=[Lithfengel, mentor of Draebor and child of emerald, was one of our finest scholars.  When most of us were still too afraid to go near a portal, he recovered an intact one and began to pry apart its secrets, in hopes of reaching Eyal.  His data showed that although this portal was still technically connected to Eyal, the link between the two worlds was still fluctuating far too much to make it safe for travel, the still-raging flames threatening to tear any prospective passengers apart before they reached their destination.  Rather than try to repair the link directly, he went into his lab and didn't emerge for a few days; when he came out, he glowed with a strange new enchantment, proclaiming it would adaptively mutate him to endure whatever damage the portal would otherwise inflict.  Saying that the consequences of failure were too awful to risk inflicting on other test subjects, he entered the portal himself, promising to return immediately after he arrived; he has not been seen since.  May he rest in peace for his selfless devotion.]=]

484: 	name = _t"demon statue: Rogroth, Eater of Souls",
485: 	lore = _t[=[Recently, the cultists of Shasshhiy'Kaish have begun speaking of a "demon seed," a sort of magical cluster of life-essence which can be implanted in a sentient being, allowing it to grow inside of them and eventually become one of our citizens.  Inspired by this idea, the children of emerald have developed a prototype of this form of magic, and the children of onyx have made a chassis to carry it into combat.  Rogroth generates countless essence-less seeds from within its frame, then embeds them in nearby living beings, so when they expire, their life-essence goes directly into the seed and allows it to grow.  We have not yet perfected its production capabilities, so currently the seeds will only become degenerate husks when they grow, but fear not!  As we get data from the tests of this design, we'll improve on it, and soon the slaughter of our foes will cause wretchlings, quasits, and even thaurheregs to spring up from their corpses.  With a little bit of luck and some decisive early skirmishes, we could even bypass the problem of getting an invasion force to the surface entirely, growing it there instead.]=]

491: 	name = _t"demon statue: Corrupted Daelach",
492: 	lore = _t[=[One of the problems with making daelach is the inherent instability that comes from creating something that is almost entirely made of magic.  If ambient levels of blight are even slightly too high, it can set off a chain reaction that at best destroys the daelach, and at worst destroys most of the mages who were building it.  Daelach production is thus theoretically cheap, but in practice involves great expense, and usually a blighted daelach has to be immediately put down lest it cause tremendous damage.  One specimen, though, adapted to the blight in a very interesting way, sprouting wings and bolstering its usual firestorms with blight, but otherwise remaining perfectly balanced and controllable.  We'll try to recreate this happy accident however we can, but in the meantime, it will prove effective on the surface of Eyal.]=]

497: 	category = "Ashes of Urh'Rok", always_pop = true,
498: 	name = _t"demon statue: Harkor'Zun",
499: 	lore = _t[=[Of the anomalies and phenomena we've noticed in our studies of the shield protecting Eyal, none have frustrated us so much as meteors.  Certain powerful Eyalite spellcasters can pull a large meteor into low orbit, passing it through the shield relatively unharmed, aside from being split into predictably-sized chunks, which are then called to the surface one-by-one in a series of devastating meteoric crashes.  While we have not yet found a way to reverse-engineer these spells to protect our standard troops from disintegration, we have had some limited success in making a construct that closely resembles a meteor in composition and appearance.  Harkor'Zun, a being made mostly of stone, was simply dropped from our platform; the shield shattered him as expected, but we had designed him to survive this, the fragments merging back into their completed form once he reached the surface.  It would seem, though, that either we made him to be too sturdy, or the shield envelops incoming objects in a sort of anti-magic coating, as he has been unable to start the second stage of this process, wherein he merges these fragments back into a completed form.  Should an Eyalite stumble upon him and attempt to destroy the fragments, Harkor'Zun will be able to re-combine and "thank" whoever granted him his ascension.]=]
500: }

We've sent out a signal of our own to intercept this, and redirect it to our platform, where <?=player:he_she()?> will be safely secured, punished for <?=player:his_her()?> disobedience, then once again exposed to a Tablet of Enlightenment to regain <?=player:his_her()?> servitude.
154: 
155: That said, given that <?=player:he_she()?> has increased dramatically in power since <?=player:his_her()?> escape, it is crucial that we keep proper tactics in mind.  Having been exposed to our alteration magic, <?=player:he_she()?> is very formidable in direct melee combat, and in the event that we cannot procure proper warding against this magic before <?=player:his_her()?> arrival, <?=player:he_she()?> can cause significant damage if not properly handled.  Under no circumstances should we let <?=player:him_her()?> run rampant in our back line; furthermore, if we simply try to lure <?=player:him_her()?> into a narrow corridor, we will not be able to bring enough firepower to bear before <?=player:he_she()?> can break through our obstructions. 295: 	lore = _t[=[Behold, the humble wretchling, a testament to our devotion to our Father!  These children of emerald were among the first to alter themselves for our quest for vengeance, and managed an astounding degree of success.  With their bursts of blinding speed, overwhelming numbers, and skin that can release prodigious amounts of corrosive fluid, wretchlings can storm onto the battlefield and pounce on our foes one-by-one, dissolving the ground they walk on while leaving them helpless against our onslaught.  Wretchlings will readily give their lives in combat, serving as obstructions and shields while their acid and our casters do their work, and still remain the most populous of our species thanks to their incredible birth rates.  It is rare to see a wretchling survive to maturity, but make no mistake - every wretchling that fights does an incredible service to our cause.]=]

301: 	name = _t"demon statue: fire imp",
302: 	lore = _t[=[If the Wretchling speaks to our worship, the Fire Imp speaks to our commitment and loyalty.  When a child of ruby goes out onto the battlefield, she fuses some of the Eyal-scarred earth from our planet to her hands, having perfected a type of magic that uses the raging magic contained within to blast our foes with the fires they've caused.  Aside from this means of appropriate justice being pleasing to Urh'Rok (as he showed when dealing with the dust-mages), it shows how dedicated we are to our cause: without hands, there's very little a Fire Imp would be able to do if she deserted or became demoralized.  Fighting and destroying is what we live for, and what better way to show it than making oneself unable to do anything but fight and destroy?  Although the bulk of the ruby species do not pursue this path, instead focusing on magical research and furthering our alteration projects, the example that the Fire Imp sets is a shining standard of commitment for all of Urh'Rok's children.]=]

485: 	lore = _t[=[Recently, the cultists of Shasshhiy'Kaish have begun speaking of a "demon seed," a sort of magical cluster of life-essence which can be implanted in a sentient being, allowing it to grow inside of them and eventually become one of our citizens.  Inspired by this idea, the children of emerald have developed a prototype of this form of magic, and the children of onyx have made a chassis to carry it into combat.  Rogroth generates countless essence-less seeds from within its frame, then embeds them in nearby living beings, so when they expire, their life-essence goes directly into the seed and allows it to grow.  We have not yet perfected its production capabilities, so currently the seeds will only become degenerate husks when they grow, but fear not!  As we get data from the tests of this design, we'll improve on it, and soon the slaughter of our foes will cause wretchlings, quasits, and even thaurheregs to spring up from their corpses.  With a little bit of luck and some decisive early skirmishes, we could even bypass the problem of getting an invasion force to the surface entirely, growing it there instead.]=]

488: newLore{

491: 	name = _t"demon statue: Corrupted Daelach",
492: 	lore = _t[=[One of the problems with making daelach is the inherent instability that comes from creating something that is almost entirely made of magic.  If ambient levels of blight are even slightly too high, it can set off a chain reaction that at best destroys the daelach, and at worst destroys most of the mages who were building it.  Daelach production is thus theoretically cheap, but in practice involves great expense, and usually a blighted daelach has to be immediately put down lest it cause tremendous damage.  One specimen, though, adapted to the blight in a very interesting way, sprouting wings and bolstering its usual firestorms with blight, but otherwise remaining perfectly balanced and controllable.  We'll try to recreate this happy accident however we can, but in the meantime, it will prove effective on the surface of Eyal.]=]

81: 	getDam = function(self, t)
82: 		-- Dont want double scaling. Ugh
83: 		local old = self.talents[t.id]
84: 		self.talents[t.id] = 1
85: 		local v
86: 		pcall(function() v = self:combatTalentSpellDamage(t, 20, 200) / 10 end) -- So paranoid
87: 		self.talents[t.id] = old
88: 		return v or 1

91: 		local tg = self:getTalentTarget(t)
92: 		local x, y, target = self:getTargetLimited(tg)

94: 		local eff = target:hasEffect(target.EFF_BLEAK_OUTCOME)
95: 
96: 		local remove = math.min(eff.stacks, t:_getStack(self))
97: 		eff.stacks = eff.stacks - remove
98: 		if eff.stacks <= 0 then target:removeEffect(target.EFF_BLEAK_OUTCOME) end
99: 
100: 		self:setEffect(self.EFF_GRIM_FUTURE, 6, {power=remove * 4})
101: 		self.turn_procs.dont_apply_bleak_outcome = true
102: 		DamageType:get(DamageType.DARKNESS).projector(self, x, y, DamageType.DARKNESS, self:spellCrit(t:_getDam(self)) * remove)
103: 		self.turn_procs.dont_apply_bleak_outcome = nil
104: 		game.level.map:particleEmitter(self.x, self.y, tg.range, "grim_future", {tx=x-self.x, ty=y-self.y})
105: 		return true
106: 	end,
107: 	info = function(self, t)
108: 		return ([[The future looks grim indeed... for your foes.
109: 		You can target a creature affected by Bleak Outcome to consume up to %s stacks, dealing %0.2f darkness damage to it for every stack and increasing your Spellpower by 4 per stacks for 6 turns.
110: 		While powered-up you can not apply new Bleak Outcome stacks.		
111: 		Damage is based on your Spellpower.]]):
112: 		tformat(t.getStack(self, t), damDesc(self, DamageType.DARKNESS, t.getDam(self, t)))

195: newEffect{
196: 	name = "INFERNAL_FEAR", image = "talents/horrifying_blows.png",
197: 	desc = _t"Overwhelming Fear",
198: 	long_desc = function(self, eff) return ("The target is losing faith that it can defeat you, reducing its damage by %d%% and slowing it by %d%%"):tformat(eff.power*eff.stacks, eff.slow_power*eff.stacks*100) end,
199: 	type = "mental",
200: 	subtype = { corruption=true },
201: 	parameters = { power=-3, max_stacks = 8, max_distance = 5, slow_power = 0, stacks = 1  },
202: 	on_gain = function(self, err) return _t"#Target# begins to fear you." end,
203: 	on_lose = function(self, err) return _t"#Target#'s shakes the fear off." end,
204: 	charges = function(self, eff) return eff.stacks or 1 end,
205: 	activate = function(self, eff)
206: 		eff.stack1 = self:addTemporaryValue("numbed", eff.power*eff.stacks)
207: 		if eff.slow_power ~= 0 then eff.stack2 = self:addTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", eff.slow_power*eff.stacks) end
208: 		
209: 		if eff.stacks >= eff.max_stacks then
210: 			eff.particle = self:addParticles(Particles.new("wildfire", 1))
211: 		else
212: 			eff.particle = self:addParticles(Particles.new("darkness_shield", 1))
213: 		end
214: 		
215: 	end,
216: 	on_merge = function(self, old_eff, new_eff)
217: 		old_eff.dur = new_eff.dur
218: 		
219: 		local stackCount = old_eff.stacks + new_eff.stacks
220: 		if stackCount >= old_eff.max_stacks then 
221: 			stackCount = old_eff.max_stacks
222: 			if old_eff.particle then self:removeParticles(old_eff.particle) end
223: 			old_eff.particle = self:addParticles(Particles.new("wildfire", 1))
224: 		end
225: 		
226: 		self:removeTemporaryValue("numbed", old_eff.stack1)
227: 		if old_eff.stack2 then self:removeTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", old_eff.stack2) end
228: 		old_eff.stack2 = nil
229: 		old_eff.stack1 = self:addTemporaryValue("numbed", old_eff.power*stackCount)
230: 		if old_eff.slow_power ~= 0 then old_eff.stack2 = self:addTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", old_eff.slow_power*stackCount) end
231: 		
232: 		old_eff.stacks = stackCount
233: 		
234: 		return old_eff
235: 		
236: 	end,
237: 	deactivate = function(self, eff)		
238: 		self:removeTemporaryValue("numbed", eff.stack1)
239: 		if eff.stack2 then self:removeTemporaryValue("global_speed_add", eff.stack2) end
240: 		if eff.particle then self:removeParticles(eff.particle) end
241: 		
242: 	end,
243: 	on_timeout = function(self, eff)
244: 		if not self.x or not eff.src.x then return end
245: 		-- Check for distance to source and reduce duration if greater than max_distance
246: 		local distance = core.fov.distance(self.x, self.y, eff.src.x, eff.src.y)
247: 		if distance > eff.max_distance then
248: 			eff.dur = eff.dur - 1
249: 		end
250: 	end,
251: }

264: function _M:login()
265: 	if self.c_login.text:len() < 2 then
266: 		Dialog:simplePopup(_t"Username", _t"Your username is too short")
267: 		return
268: 	end
269: 	if self.c_pass.text:len() < 4 then
270: 		Dialog:simplePopup(_t"Password", _t"Your password is too short")
271: 		return
272: 	end
273: 	game:createProfile({create=false, login=self.c_login.text, pass=self.c_pass.text})
274: end

59: 				end) end,
60: 			})
61: 		end},
62: 	}
63: }

1002: 	define_as = "ROD_ENTROPY",
1003: 	unided_name = _t"light sucking rod", image = "object/artifact/rod_of_entropy.png",
1004: 	name = "Rod of Entropy", color=colors.PURPLE, unique=true,
1005: 	desc = _t[[This rod seems to make light die around it. You feel tired just looking at it.]],
1006: 	cost = 200,
1007: 	level_range = {8, 20},
1008: 	rarity = 200,
1009: 	material_level = 2,
1010: 	max_power = 75, power_regen = 1,
1011: 	carrier = {
1012: 		lite = -1,
1013: 	},
1014: 	use_power = {
1015: 		name = function(self, who) return ("temporarily causes the target to receive entropic backlash from any healing they receive for %d turns up to %d%% of the healing done. This effect scales with your Magic stat."):
1016: 			tformat(self.use_power.duration, self.use_power.getpower(self, who))
1017: 		end,
1018: 		getpower = function(self, who) return 50 + who:getMag() end,
1019: 		power = 75,
1020: 		duration = 6,
1021: 		range = 7,
1022: 		requires_target = true,
1023: 		target = function(self, who) return {type="bolt", range=self.use_power.range} end,
1024: 		tactical = { ANNOY = 1 },
1025: 		use = function(self, who)
1026: 			local tg = self.use_power.target(self, who)
1027: 			local x, y = who:getTarget(tg)
1028: 			if not x or not y then return nil end
1029: 			game.logSeen(who, "%s activates %s %s!", who:getName():capitalize(), who:his_her(), self:getName({no_add_name = true, do_color = true}))
1030: 			who:project(tg, x, y, function(px, py)
1031: 				local target = game.level.map(px, py, engine.Map.ACTOR)
1032: 				if not target then return end
1033: 				target:setEffect(target.EFF_ENTROPIC_ROD, 10, {src=who, power=self.use_power.getpower(self, who), apply_power=who:combatSpellpower()})
1034: 			end, 1, {type="slime"})
1035: 			return {id=true, used=true}
1036: 		end
1037: 	},
1038: }

38: 	id = "cults-cultist-unlock-intro",
39: 	category = "Forbidden Cults", always_pop = true,
40: 	name = _t"Lessons of Inevitability - Introduction",
41: 	lore = _t[[In the Age of Dusk, it seemed that the world was ending to many of Eyal's inhabitants. The destruction caused by the Spellblaze left the land withered and scorched. Food was scarce, disease was rampant and everyone was desperate. For a select few, their salvation came from an unlikely visitor. An entity they simply came to knew as The Teacher visited Eyal from somewhere beyond the stars, emerging from an ancient Sher'tul farportal. It discovered a group of survivors in the depths of Eyal which begged it for knowledge, anything they could use as a weapon against the horrors ravaging their world.
42: 
43: Out of charity and kindness, it agreed to teach them how to wield the power of entropy itself. However, it made it clear to them that this was not a power to be taken lightly and could very well bring about their doom. As desperate as they were, all of them agreed without a second thought, heedless of the consequences it could have.
44: 
45: Hithre was one of The Teacher's pupils, a Shalore who became one of the first to wield entropic magic in the entirety of Eyal.]],
46: }

50: 	category = "Forbidden Cults", always_pop = true,
51: 	name = _t"Lessons of Inevitability - Entropic Backlash and Healing",
52: 	lore = _t[[My first lesson to you, my students, is to understand what it means to wield entropy. When using its power, it's impossible to escape its withering touch. Your bodies will suffer from the backlash of your spells and carry a residue of those energies at all times. As such, your ability to recover from wounds and injury will be significantly impaired. However, you can learn to resist this backlash and even manipulate the threads of fate to pass it on to your enemies.
53: 
54: #{italic}#Go check your new spell for detailed information.#{normal}#]],

59: 	name = _t"Lessons of Inevitability - Netherblast",
60: 	lore = _t[[For this exercise, you will learn how to manipulate and direct entropic energies. This spell will be your main defence against your foes and will teach you to manage the backlash from using it. Few beings in existence are capable of defending themselves against the Netherblast, so practice with it frequently until you have perfected it.
61: 
62: #{italic}#Go check your new spell for detailed information.#{normal}#]],
63: }
64: newLore{
65: 	id = "cults-cultist-unlock-lesson-3",

67: 	name = _t"Lessons of Inevitability - Fatebreaker",
68: 	lore = _t[[This spell will be the most important you will learn from me. Fate is a force made up of many threads. Provided that you understand how the threads all connect to each other, you can manipulate it to your own ends. This spell will allow you to pass on doomed threads from you onto your opponents, escaping from your own preordained death. Remember that this spell should not be used lightly and that some threads do not bend to anyone's will, no matter how hard you pull.
69: 
70: The target dummies have been imbued with fake void energies; use your Fatebreaker on them and then use Netherblast on yourself while low on life. This is a difficult exercise, students. Be aware that you are now risking your life if you execute it wrong.
71: 
72: #{italic}#Go check your new spell for detailed information.#{normal}#]],
73: }

78: 	lore = _t[[The building blocks of all things are held together by innumerable laws. These very laws govern all of reality and are set in stone, in most cases. With proper use of your magic, it's entirely possible to sever these bonds and defy these laws, unraveling your foe's very existence. Not only is your opponent affected by this, but the area around them is too. It creates cracks in reality which allow things to slip through. You must use this moment to call out into the void and bring forth creatures to assist you in battle.

80: I am somewhat hesitant to teach this spell, but all of you have been performing admirably. You [i]must[/i] not use this spell lightly. Have a clear image in your head of what you wish to summon or you will be putting yourself at the mercy of the void. There are countless entities which live between the stars, many of which are mindless and pitiless things.
81: 
82: Please all focus your attention on the central target dummy. Hithre you will cast Netherblast at it to keep Nihil on it while the other students will use a Dark Whisper spell on it.
83: 
84: #{italic}#Go check your new spells for detailed information.#{normal}#]],

The ones who learned this forbidden lore became known as the Cultists of Entropy.

106: newLore{
107: 	id = "races-krog",
108: 	category = "races",
109: 	name = _t"Loremaster Greynot's Analysis of the Races - Chapter 12 - Krogs",
110: 	lore = _t[[The krog are perhaps the youngest of the intelligent races of Maj'Eyal, only coming into existence recently. They claim that they were formerly ogres that have had their runes removed, somehow surviving having their runes replaced by a combination of natural infusions and drakes blood. The removal of their runes was orchestrated by the Ziguranth, who apparently decided action needed to be taken to prevent all ogres from being horribly and brutally killed as a result of the Spellhunt, leading to the creation of the krog. The official reasons given by the Ziguranth for this action was that the ogres were unfortunate victims of magic rather then perpetrators of it, and the Ziguranth were just looking to help to free them from the taint of the arcane.
111: 
112: Due to the fact that they were originally ogres, it comes as no surprise that the two races share much with each other. They tend to have similar hair coloring, facial features, and other similar traits. The average krog is a bit shorter then a ogre at 8'2" and perhaps a little leaner, but otherwise the rest of their body dimensions remain the same. One would likely be hard pressed to distinguish a krog from an ogre or vice versa if it wasn't for the heavy tint of greens and browns within their eyes and skin, likely a side effect of whatever natural process the Ziguranth employed to strip them of their runes.
113: 
114: The majority of the krog tend to live in or around the middle of the continent where the heart of Ziguranth territory lies and they have been known to take up arms in service to the anti-magic cause. Indeed one may find that the majority of any Ziguranth Patrol one may encounter is usually made up of krog fighters. All krog seem to demonstrate some connection to nature as well as possessing abilities to combat mages, not to mention harbor a huge hatred towards anyone that deals with magic in any way. Indeed, a krog's disdain for the arcane begs the question if perhaps the Ziguranth did a bit more then just remove the runes from their bodies.
115: 
116: Commonly when they are not in the employ of the Ziguranth, or otherwise answering the call to do battle with a rogue mage, the krog have been known to contract themselves out as laborers to whomever may hire them. Like ogres, krog are also known for having impressive appetites and one can find many krog farmers plowing fields to grow food for themselves to eat. They are also known for their talents in mixing infusions, producing the majority of what one might find in the markets around the continent.
117: 
118: Of course no analysis of the krog would be complete without mentioning the many stories, songs, and artwork that revolve around their many pursuits. A lot of encouragement is directed at younger krogs by their peers to venture out into the world and perform heroic deeds. This course of action seems less to do with valor, glory, or riches; something one might expect of a typical 'adventurer' and more to do with the mistrust that followed them formerly being ogres. In an effort to combat their initial image they had as former ogres, the krog sought to commit themselves to gaining a new image through achievement of impressive feats. To this end they seem to have been rather successful as evidenced by the creation of the many artistic works told about them. ]]}

120: newLore{
121: 	id = "races-drem",
122: 	category = "races",
123: 	name = _t"Loremaster Greynot's Analysis of the Races - Chapter 13 - Drems",
124: 	lore = _t[[Eyal's underground is abundant with strange, and not particularly wholesome, creatures. Many of them are mindless monstrosities, unable to be reasoned with and best left alone. However, perhaps the most unusual of these creatures are the Drem. For the longest time, Drem were presumed to simply be another form of horror which dwelled in Eyal's underground. The recent emergence of thinking Drem, however, has forced many scholars to reassess their race as a whole.
125: 
126: A Drem is roughly the same height as a Dwarf and has a vaguely similar facial structure as well. This is where the similarities between the two races tend to end. Drem have no distinguishing facial features and are incapable of growing beards like dwarves, instead growing wiry and unkempt patches of hair which vary greatly in thickness. Due to the lack of facial features such as eyes, ears, a mouth and a nose, it is not currently known how a Drem eats or how they sense things around them. The mental faculties of thinking Drem seems to vary wildly from each individual as well. Some are barely more capable of rational thought than feral Drem, while others have gained intellect comparable to the brightest minds of Eyal.
127: 
128: As they have only recently come out of their previously mindless states, the Drem are a people who are completely disconnected with the world around them. They possess no cultural identity or history to fall back on and sit on the precipice between the civilised races of Eyal's surface and the horrors of Eyal's underground. Many suspect that they possess some connection to the dwarves, the prevailing theory being that they are some sort of corrupted offshoot of that proud race. There has been little research into the subject and little evidence found to substantiate these claims, however. What impact the Drem will have on Eyal's future can only be speculated upon at this point.]]}

49: 	name = _t"page from a logbook (3)",
50: 	lore = _t[[The whispers... Even as I'm running away, the whispers don't stop. It echoes over and over again. I can feel the walls of my mind crumbling down. It wants me to go back. I won't go back, not after what happened. All of them died, melted and devoured, broken and torn asunder... The writhing mass, the endless aberrant things... One drake towered above them all. It whispered to me, just like in my dreams... It had no eyes, but it looked right through me. All of my mortal emotions, thoughts and dreams were laid bare before its hideous visage... And it laughed. It laughed with a horrid, psychic shriek.
51: 
52: It wants me to go back. It wants me to return so it can finish what it started. No, no, no. I must write this report. Tell the Ziguranth. I must send this away, I... I... I must go back it wants me to go back I-I-I [i](Nothing but a series of erratic and completely incoherent scribblings follow. Judging by where you found this letter, he did not make it back to Zigur.)[/i] ]],

58: 	name = _t"entropic void",
59: 	lore = _t[[It's cold. Terribly cold. The unreality around you seems to be draining you slowly, making your body lock up and your limbs go stiff. There is entropy at work here, but you can see small patches of light defiantly standing out against the darkness. The warm glow infuses you with vigour, driving away the terrible cold. There must be an antropic force at work here, the only thing which can defeat entropy. You can plainly see that it is fighting a losing battle.

61: As you get your bearings, you can sense that there is something in here with you. Its presence looms over this entire void, filling you with a primordial sense of dread. The battle that will be fought here will be unlike any you have been through. And perhaps it will be your last.]],

74: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
75: 	name = _t"a new threat (1)",
76: 	lore = _t[[Long have we dwelt in the earth, the light of the surface never touching our sanctuary. We have sought power which few can even guess at and learned to wield the power of the dark ones squirming in the void. But, after our long seclusion, a creature from the depths has come to destroy our fortress. This 'maggot' is a creature which consumes anything in front of it, sliding through the earth and carving a path of destruction. This shall be where it stops. With the power we have gathered, we shall slay this intruder.
77: 
78: While the hide of the creature has proven too tough to break through, we have devised a clever method to rid ourselves of it. By feeding it a special artifact, we shall be able to open a portal directly into its soft, vulnerable insides. May it taste the results of our research.]],

85: 	lore = _t[[We have managed to enter the beast. Alas, we were not prepared for the creature itself to have natural defences. Pieces of its own flesh came to destroy us. We called upon the dark beyond and it answered, withering the Maggot's flesh right in front of our eyes! But, for all of our power, the flesh kept coming. A lot of researchers were lost.
86: 
87: It seems that it falls to me alone to deal with this creature. Only my entropic power could hope to put an end to it. The density of its fleshling defenders grows and grows as we push our way to the creature's brain. If we destroy that, then this will be over in an instant.]],

94: 	lore = _t[[We have been trapped inside the maggot for a few days now. I'm the only one who seems to be still set on destroying this creature. Those that remain here conspire against me. I hear them whisper among themselves. They intend to abandon me and make their way back to the portal, which is surely swarming with defenders by now. Tomorrow, I will goad them into following me for one last charge. We would have a better chance at going for the brain than we would getting back to the portal.

111: 	lore = _t[[You ever gotten yourself into a mess that you didn't know how to get out of? Well, that's kind of where I'm at right now. This thing, whatever it is, just burst out of the ground and swallowed me whole. Normally a girl has to get offered on an altar to monsters to get eaten like this, but it looks like this one just took a fancy to me.
112: 
113: I've seen a lot of things. Undead, horrors, sometimes a bear with psychic powers, but whatever this thing is, it's in a league of its own. It's like I'm inside a snake with the way it winds and how long it is. Sometimes these meaty bits of something come after me and have acid pouring out of them... I get the impression that it's trying to digest me. I've managed to make a little hideout in one of the folds of its belly, but I don't know how long these protective runes are going to last.
114: 
115: So, I guess my plan is to find a way out of here or to take this thing down with me. For most things, food goes in one end and... Well, you know the rest. But this thing... It just flat out digests everything it swallows. I've watched those things breaking down entire chunks of rock, houses, enough trees to fill a forest... This thing can eat pretty much everything.
116: 
117: With that in mind, my only option is to kill it from the inside. Dunno how I'm going to do that just yet.]],

131: 	lore = function() return ([[Being an adventurer is supposed to be fun. You know, get out there, kill a couple monsters, grab some loot, spend all the loot money you made and repeat. There's always something new out there to plunder, if you get in there before everyone else. But sometimes, people like to lock their loot behind dumb puzzles. Like this one. I've been sitting here just trying different combinations in this thing. All day, all night, different combinations. The way this stupid thing works doesn't make any sense at all! Most people who make puzzles like these usually leave some hints, but I've got nothing to work with!

That way I can keep track of what works and what doesn't. There had better be an amazing reward for all this work...

173: newLore{
174: 	id = "cults-illusory-castle-1",
175: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
176: 	name = _t"an escape from reality (1)",
177: 	lore = _t[[So, what does an adventurer do when they get bored with it all? For me, I wanted to find a nice castle somewhere out in the countryside and spend the rest of my days in idle contentment. The issue there is that I made a lot of enemies who would have loved for me to settle down in one spot, so I needed to think of a solution.
178: 
179: That's when I found this place. Everyone else avoided it because people never left once they went inside it. Being used to the adventuring life, I saw such a thing as a challenge. Turns out that this cursed castle, as people referred to it, constantly changes its inside layout. No one really knows how or why it does it, but I'm not really one to question such things. If I could just work out the logic behind how it shifted itself, I could have an unassailable fortress. 
180: 
181: However, I also found that this still didn't deter people from coming to kill me. They all swarmed in and although a lot of them got lost in the hallways, a few actually managed to reach me. I had grown rather attached to the place at this point, but neither could I stay there. My solution came with a bizarre tome I had found in my adventures. When I opened the cover and pointed it in the right direction, it could suck things into its very pages.
182: 
183: So, being the savvy adventurer I am, I opened the tome and sucked the entire castle inside of it. It seems like the tome could only suck so much inside its covers, so it could no longer hold anything else in it. Although I had to sacrifice a great treasure, I now had a sanctuary away from the real world which I could escape to whenever I needed shelter.]],
184: }

187: 	id = "cults-illusory-castle-2",
188: 	category = "Forbidden Cults",
189: 	name = _t"an escape from reality (2)",
190: 	lore = _t[[As much as I love this castle, it really does give you a headache after a while. Whenever I tried to decorate rooms or organise anything in its interior, I would inevitably find the room in a completely different area. While I can navigate through the place without too much trouble now, it's still pretty annoying when I have to find a specific room.
191: 
192: I sometimes wonder if I'll ever run into the people who entered this place and never left. The shifting rooms themselves aren't that difficult to understand, once you find out the patterns behind their changes. If I could work out, then surely someone else had to as well, right? I do sometimes feel as if I'm not really alone in the castle, despite being the only person who can even reach this place, not to mention the only living thing walking these halls. I haven't seen so much as a mouse since I trapped the castle within my book.
193: 
194: I fear that I'm also starting to develop an unhealthy attachment to this place. I have not been able to have a single day of peace since I began my adventuring career, so the security these glass walls offer is becoming far too alluring to me.]],
195: }

Animated golems made of glass wander the halls now, searching for me. My fortress is no longer mine and there is no safety to be found within these walls. I knew that I could never truly find somewhere I could be safe, not in this book or in the outside world. I do not know where these golems came from. Perhaps the castle itself is trying to expel me from it or maybe I triggered some defence by wandering into the wrong room.

111: 	lore = _t[[You ever gotten yourself into a mess that you didn't know how to get out of? Well, that's kind of where I'm at right now. This thing, whatever it is, just burst out of the ground and swallowed me whole. Normally a girl has to get offered on an altar to monsters to get eaten like this, but it looks like this one just took a fancy to me.
112: 
113: I've seen a lot of things. Undead, horrors, sometimes a bear with psychic powers, but whatever this thing is, it's in a league of its own. It's like I'm inside a snake with the way it winds and how long it is. Sometimes these meaty bits of something come after me and have acid pouring out of them... I get the impression that it's trying to digest me. I've managed to make a little hideout in one of the folds of its belly, but I don't know how long these protective runes are going to last.
114: 
115: So, I guess my plan is to find a way out of here or to take this thing down with me. For most things, food goes in one end and... Well, you know the rest. But this thing... It just flat out digests everything it swallows. I've watched those things breaking down entire chunks of rock, houses, enough trees to fill a forest... This thing can eat pretty much everything.
116: 
117: With that in mind, my only option is to kill it from the inside. Dunno how I'm going to do that just yet.]],

55: 	name = "Anarchic Walk",
56: 	type = {"demented/beyond-sanity", 2},
57: 	require = dementedreq2,
58: 	points = 5,
59: 	insanity = -15,
60: 	cooldown = 6,
61: 	tactical = { CLOSE_IN=1 },
62: 	requires_target = true,
63: 	on_pre_use = function(self, t, silent) if not (self:hasEffect(self.EFF_CHAOS_ORBS) and self:hasEffect(self.EFF_CHAOS_ORBS).stacks >= 2) then if not silent then game.logPlayer(self, "You require at least two chaos orbs.") end return false end return true end,
64: 	--range = function(self, t) return math.ceil(self:combatTalentScale(t, 3, 10)) end,
65: 	range = function(self, t) return math.ceil(self:combatTalentLimit(t, 8, 1, 5)) end,
66: 	getMax = function(self, t) return 8 end,
67: 	target = function(self, t) return {type="cone", range=0, selffire=false, radius=t.getMax(self, t), nolock=true, simple_dir_request=true} end,
68: 	action = function(self, t)
69: 		local tg = self:getTalentTarget(t)
70: 		local x, y = self:getTarget(tg)
71: 		if not x then return nil end
72: 		local range = self:getTalentRange(t)
73: 		local spots, shortspots = {}, {}
74: 		self:project(tg, x, y, function(px, py)
75: 			if self:canMove(px, py) then
76: 				if core.fov.distance(self.x, self.y, px, py) >= range then spots[#spots+1] = {x=px, y=py}
77: 				else shortspots[#shortspots+1] = {x=px, y=py} end
78: 			end
79: 		end)
80: 		if #spots == 0 then spots = shortspots end
81: 		if #spots == 0 then return nil end
82: 		local spot = rng.table(spots)
83: 
84: 		game.level.map:particleEmitter(self.x, self.y, 1, "teleport")
85: 		self:teleportRandom(spot.x, spot.y, 0)
86: 		game.level.map:particleEmitter(self.x, self.y, 1, "teleport")
87: 
88: 		self:callEffect(self.EFF_CHAOS_ORBS, "useOrb", 2)
89: 
90: 		game:playSoundNear(self, "talents/anarchic_walk")
91: 		return true
92: 	end,
93: 	info = function(self, t)
94: 		return ([[You consume the chaotic forces of 2 chaos orbs, randomly teleporting you in a general direction up to %d tiles away.
95: 		You will always travel at least %d tiles away if possible.]]):tformat(t.getMax(self, t), self:getTalentRange(t))
96: 	end,
97: }

56: 				self:setEffect(self.EFF_FORTUNE, 5, {src = self, stacks=1, max_stacks=10, power = t.getSaves(self, t), crit=t.getCrit(self,t), avoid=avoid })

Alternatively, you consider leaving before the worm arrives and finding your own purpose in the outside world.

528: 	local ok, err = self:canWearObject(o, inven.name)
529: 	if not ok then
530: 		if vocal then game.logSeen(self, "%s can not wear (%s): %s (%s).", self:getName():capitalize(), self.inven_def[inven.name].name:lower(), o_name, err) end
531: 		return false
532: 	end
533: 	if o:check("on_canwear", self, inven) then return false end
534: 	local offslot, stackable = self:getObjectOffslot(o), o:stackable()
535: 	local added, slot, stack = self:addObject(inven_id, o, nil, force_item)
536: 
537: 	if added then
538: 		if vocal then game.logSeen(self, "%s wears: %s.", self:getName():capitalize(), o_name) end
539: 		return true, stack
540: 	elseif not force_inven and offslot and self:getInven(offslot) and #(self:getInven(offslot)) < self:getInven(offslot).max and self:canWearObject(o, offslot) then
541: 		if vocal then game.logSeen(self, "%s wears (offslot): %s.", self:getName():capitalize(), o:getName{do_color=true}) end
542: 		added, slot, stack = self:addObject(offslot, o)
543: 		return added, stack
544: 	elseif replace then -- no room but replacement is allowed
545: 		local ro = self:takeoffObject(inven_id, force_item or 1)
546: 		if not ro then return false end
547: 		-- Check if we still can wear it, to prevent the replace-abuse
548: 		local ok, err = self:canWearObject(o, inven.name)
549: 		if not ok then
550: 			if vocal then game.logSeen(self, "%s can not wear (%s): %s (%s).", self:getName():capitalize(), self.inven_def[inven.name].name:lower(), o_name, err) end
551: 			if ro then self:addObject(inven_id, ro, true, force_item) end
552: 			return false
553: 		end
554: 		added, slot, stack = self:addObject(inven_id, o, nil, force_item)
555: 		if vocal then game.logSeen(self, "%s wears (replacing %s): %s.", self:getName():capitalize(), ro:getName{do_color=true}, o_name) end
556: 		if stack and ro:stack(stack) then -- stack remaining stack with old if possible (ignores stack limits)
557: 			stack = nil
558: 		end
559: 		return ro, stack -- caller handles the replaced object and remaining stack if any
560: 	else
561: 		if vocal then game.logSeen(self, "%s can not wear: %s.", self:getName():capitalize(), o:getName{do_color=true}) end
562: 		return false
563: 	end

616: --- Re-order inventory, sorting and stacking it
617: -- sort order is type > subtype > name > getNumber()
618: function _M:sortInven(inven)
619: 	if not inven then inven = self.inven[self.INVEN_INVEN] end
620: 	inven = self:getInven(inven)
621: 	if not inven then return end
622: --	local stacked, last, stacklimit = false, false, inven.stack_limit or math.huge
623: 	local stacked, last, stacklimit = false, false, self:invenStackLimit(inven)
624: 
625: 	-- First, stack objects from top
626: 	for i = 1, #inven do
627: 		if not inven[i] then break end
628: 		-- If it is stackable, look for objects after it that can stack into it
629: 		if inven[i]:stackable() then
630: 			for j = #inven, i + 1, -1 do
631: 			-- check stack limit
632: 				stacked, last = inven[i]:stack(inven[j], false, stacklimit - inven[i]:getNumber())
633: 				if stacked then
634: 					if last then
635: 						table.remove(inven, j)
636: 					else
637: 						break
638: 					end
639: 				end
640: 			end
641: 		end
642: 	end
643: 
644: 	-- Sort them
645: 	table.sort(inven, function(a, b)
646: 		local ta, tb = a:getTypeOrder(), b:getTypeOrder()
647: 		local sa, sb = a:getSubtypeOrder(), b:getSubtypeOrder()
648: 		if ta == tb then
649: 			if sa == sb then
650: 				if a.name == b.name then
651: 					return a:getNumber() > b:getNumber()
652: 				else
653: 					return a.name < b.name
654: 				end
655: 			else
656: 				return sa < sb
657: 			end
658: 		else
659: 			return ta < tb
660: 		end
661: 	end)
662: 	self.changed = true
663: end

738: --- Checks if the talent can be learned
739: -- @param t the talent to check
740: -- @param offset the level offset to check, defaults to 1
741: -- @param ignore_special ignore requirement of special
742: function _M:canLearnTalent(t, offset, ignore_special)
743: 	-- Check prerequisites
744: 	if rawget(t, "require") then
745: 		local req = t.require
746: 		if type(req) == "function" then req = req(self, t) end
747: 		local tlev = self:getTalentLevelRaw(t) + (offset or 1)
748: 
749: 		-- Obviously this requires the ActorStats interface
750: 		if req.stat then
751: 			for s, v in pairs(req.stat) do
752: 				v = util.getval(v, tlev)
753: 				if self:getStat(s) < v then return nil, ("not enough stat: %s"):tformat(s:upper()) end
754: 			end
755: 		end
756: 		if req.level then
757: 			if self.level < util.getval(req.level, tlev) then
758: 				return nil, _t"not enough levels"
759: 			end
760: 		end
761: 		if req.special and not ignore_special then
762: 			if not req.special.fct(self, t, offset) then
763: 				return nil, req.special.desc
764: 			end
765: 		end
766: 		if req.special2 and not ignore_special then
767: 			if not req.special2.fct(self, t, offset) then
768: 				return nil, req.special2.desc
769: 			end
770: 		end
771: 		if req.special3 and not ignore_special then
772: 			if not req.special3.fct(self, t, offset) then
773: 				return nil, req.special3.desc
774: 			end
775: 		end
776: 		if req.talent then
777: 			for _, tid in ipairs(req.talent) do
778: 				if type(tid) == "table" then
779: 					if type(tid[2]) == "boolean" and tid[2] == false then
780: 						if self:knowTalent(tid[1]) then return nil, _t"missing dependency" end
781: 					else
782: 						if self:getTalentLevelRaw(tid[1]) < tid[2] then return nil, _t"missing dependency" end
783: 					end
784: 				else
785: 					if not self:knowTalent(tid) then return nil, _t"missing dependency" end
786: 				end
787: 			end
788: 		end
789: 		if req.birth_descriptors then
790: 			for _, d in ipairs(req.birth_descriptors) do
791: 				if not self.descriptor or self.descriptor[d[1]] ~= d[2] then return nil, ("is not %s"):tformat(_t(d[2])) end
792: 			end
793: 		end
794: 	end
795: 
796: 	if not self:knowTalentType(t.type[1]) and not t.type_no_req then return nil, _t"unknown talent type" end
797: 
798: 	-- Check talent type
799: 	local known = self:numberKnownTalent(t.type[1], t.id, t.type[2])
800: 	if t.type[2] and known < t.type[2] - 1 then
801: 		return nil, _t"not enough talents of this type known"
802: 	end
803: 
804: 	-- Ok!
805: 	return true
806: end

808: --- Formats the requirements as a (multiline) string
809: -- @param t_id the id of the talent to desc
810: -- @param levmod a number (1 should be the smartest) to add to current talent level to display requirements, defaults to 0
811: function _M:getTalentReqDesc(t_id, levmod)
812: 	local t = _M.talents_def[t_id]
813: 	local req = t.require
814: 	if not req then return tstring{}, nil end
815: 	if type(req) == "function" then req = req(self, t) end
816: 
817: 	local tlev = self:getTalentLevelRaw(t_id) + (levmod or 0)
818: 
819: 	local str = tstring{}
820: 
821: 	if not t.type_no_req then
822: 		str:add((self:knowTalentType(t.type[1]) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}), _t"- Talent category known", true)
823: 	end
824: 
825: 	if t.type[2] and t.type[2] > 1 then
826: 		local known = self:numberKnownTalent(t.type[1], t.id, t.type[2])
827: 		local c = (known >= t.type[2] - 1) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
828: 		str:add(c, ("- Lower talents of the same category: %d"):tformat(t.type[2] - 1), true)
829: 	end
830: 
831: 	-- Obviously this requires the ActorStats interface
832: 	if req.stat then
833: 		for s, v in pairs(req.stat) do
834: 			v = util.getval(v, tlev)
835: 			local c = (self:getStat(s) >= v) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
836: 			str:add(c, ("- %s %d"):format(self.stats_def[s].name, v), true)
837: 		end
838: 	end
839: 	if req.level then
840: 		local v = util.getval(req.level, tlev)
841: 		local c = (self.level >= v) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
842: 		str:add(c, ("- Level %d"):tformat(v), true)
843: 	end
844: 	if req.special then
845: 		local c = (req.special.fct(self, t, offset)) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
846: 		str:add(c, ("- %s"):format(req.special.desc), true)
847: 	end
848: 	if req.special2 then
849: 		local c = (req.special2.fct(self, t, offset)) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
850: 		str:add(c, ("- %s"):format(req.special2.desc), true)
851: 	end
852: 	if req.special3 then
853: 		local c = (req.special3.fct(self, t, offset)) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
854: 		str:add(c, ("- %s"):format(req.special3.desc), true)
855: 	end
856: 	if req.talent then
857: 		for _, tid in ipairs(req.talent) do
858: 			if type(tid) == "table" then
859: 				if type(tid[2]) == "boolean" and tid[2] == false then
860: 					local c = (not self:knowTalent(tid[1])) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
861: 					str:add(c, ("- Talent %s (not known)"):tformat(self:getTalentFromId(tid[1]).name), true)
862: 				else
863: 					local c = (self:getTalentLevelRaw(tid[1]) >= tid[2]) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
864: 					str:add(c, ("- Talent %s (%d)"):tformat(self:getTalentFromId(tid[1]).name, tid[2]), true)
865: 				end
866: 			else
867: 				local c = self:knowTalent(tid) and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
868: 				str:add(c, ("- Talent %s"):tformat(self:getTalentFromId(tid).name), true)
869: 			end
870: 		end
871: 	end
872: 	if req.birth_descriptors then
873: 		for _, d in ipairs(req.birth_descriptors) do
874: 			local c = self.descriptor and self.descriptor[d[1]] == d[2] and {"color", 0x00,0xff,0x00} or {"color", 0xff,0x00,0x00}
875: 			str:add(c, ("- Is %s"):tformat(_t(d[2])), true)
876: 		end
877: 	end
878: 
879: 	return str, req
880: end

276: function _M:loginSteam()
277: 	local d = self:simpleWaiter(_t"Login...", _t"Logging in your account, please wait...") core.display.forceRedraw()
278: 	d:timeout(10, function() Dialog:simplePopup("Steam", _t"Steam client not found.")	end)
279: 	core.steam.sessionTicket(function(ticket)
280: 		if not ticket then
281: 			Dialog:simplePopup("Steam", _t"Steam client not found.")
282: 			d:done()
283: 			return
284: 		end
285: 		profile:performloginSteam((ticket:toHex()))
286: 		profile:waitFirstAuth()
287: 		d:done()
288: 		if not profile.auth and profile.auth_last_error then
289: 			if profile.auth_last_error == "auth error" then
290: 				game:newSteamAccount()
291: 			end
292: 		end
293: 	end)
294: end

264: function _M:login()
265: 	if self.c_login.text:len() < 2 then
266: 		Dialog:simplePopup(_t"Username", _t"Your username is too short")
267: 		return
268: 	end
269: 	if self.c_pass.text:len() < 4 then
270: 		Dialog:simplePopup(_t"Password", _t"Your password is too short")
271: 		return
272: 	end
273: 	game:createProfile({create=false, login=self.c_login.text, pass=self.c_pass.text})
274: end

276: function _M:loginSteam()
277: 	local d = self:simpleWaiter(_t"Login...", _t"Logging in your account, please wait...") core.display.forceRedraw()
278: 	d:timeout(10, function() Dialog:simplePopup("Steam", _t"Steam client not found.")	end)
279: 	core.steam.sessionTicket(function(ticket)
280: 		if not ticket then
281: 			Dialog:simplePopup("Steam", _t"Steam client not found.")
282: 			d:done()
283: 			return
284: 		end
285: 		profile:performloginSteam((ticket:toHex()))
286: 		profile:waitFirstAuth()
287: 		d:done()
288: 		if not profile.auth and profile.auth_last_error then
289: 			if profile.auth_last_error == "auth error" then
290: 				game:newSteamAccount()
291: 			end
292: 		end
293: 	end)

177: 			local dam1 = who:damDesc(engine.DamageType.FIRE, self.use_power.damage1(self, who))
178: 			local dam2 = who:damDesc(engine.DamageType.FIRE, self.use_power.damage2(self, who))

187: 		tactical = {ATTACKAREA = {FIRE = 2}, CLOSEIN = 1, ESCAPE = 2},
188: 		findlanding = function(self, who, tx, ty, tg) -- find landing spot near (tx, ty)
189: --			print(("[Anti-Gravity Boots] looking for landing at (%s, %s)"):format(tx, ty))
190: 			if tx == who.x and ty == who.y and not game.level.map:checkEntity(tx, ty, engine.Map.TERRAIN, "block_move", who) then return tx, ty end

203: 			local fx, fy, grids

205: --			print(("[Anti-Gravity Boots]--%s : target selected at (%s, %s)"):format(who.name, tx, ty))

209: 				local _ _, x, y = who:canProject(tg, x, y)

214: 				local _ _, x, y = who:canProject(tg, tx, ty)
215: 				if not x or not y then return nil end
216: 				fx, fy = self.use_power.findlanding(self, who, x, y, tg)

218: 				if not fx or not fx then

223: 				if tactic == "attackarea" and core.fov.distance(fx, fy, tx, ty) > 3 then return nil end

226: 			who:logCombat(nil, "#Source# ignites %s %s, creating a #LIGHT_RED#blast of fire#LAST# that %s!", who:his_her(), self:getName({no_add_name=true, do_color=true}), fail and ("engulfs %s spectacularly"):tformat(who:him_her()) or ("launches %s in the air"):tformat(who:him_her()))

232: 			local ox, oy = who.x, who.y
